questions.q: What is kept on the call stack?
options: Every Python object ever created
One frame per function call happening right now, with its local names and where to return
The files on the disk
Only global variables
questions.explain: A frame is pushed when a function is called and popped when it returns. A traceback is the stack, printed.

questions.q: In Python, what does cart = ["Masala Box"] do?
options: Stores the list inside the variable
Creates a list object on the heap and makes the name cart point to it
Copies the list to the disk
Creates a new thread
questions.explain: Variables are names; objects live on the heap. Several names can point to the same object.

questions.q: same_cart = ashas_cart, then same_cart.append("Steel Water Bottle"). What happens to ashas_cart?
options: Nothing, it was copied
It also shows the bottle, because both names point to the same list
Python raises an error
The bottle replaces the first item
questions.explain: Assignment never copies. To copy, use list(ashas_cart), ashas_cart.copy(), or copy.deepcopy for nested data.

questions.q: def add_to_cart(item, cart=[]) — why did Ravi find Asha's Masala Box in his cart?
options: A database bug
The default list is created once, when the function is defined, and shared by every call
Python mixed up the two users' threads
The cart was saved to disk
questions.explain: Use cart=None and create a new list inside the function.

questions.q: Python has a garbage collector. How can Bazaar's price service still leak memory?
options: It can't; Python never leaks
The program keeps references to objects it will never use again, for example a cache with no limit
The garbage collector is turned off in Docker
Integers never get freed
questions.explain: Garbage collection only frees unreachable objects. Anything still in a global cache stays reachable. Bound your caches.

questions.q: A Bazaar container exits with code 137 and docker inspect says OOMKilled: true. What happened?
options: The code had a syntax error
It went over its memory limit, and the kernel's OOM killer ended it with SIGKILL
It finished normally
The network went down
questions.explain: 137 = 128 + 9 (SIGKILL). The program had no chance to print anything. Look for a memory leak.

questions.q: A category tree is 5,000 levels deep. The recursive function fails with RecursionError. What is the best fix?
options: sys.setrecursionlimit(1_000_000)
Rewrite it as a loop, which uses a single frame
Buy more RAM
Catch the error and ignore it
questions.explain: Every recursive call adds a frame. A loop doesn't. Raising the limit a lot can crash the interpreter itself.

questions.q: (Going deeper) When does CPython free an object?
options: Only when the program ends
When its reference count reaches zero, or when the cycle collector finds it unreachable
Every 10 seconds
Only when you call del on it
questions.explain: Reference counting frees most objects instantly. Objects in a reference cycle wait for the cycle collector (gc).
